features.title: What a skill is and how to add one in Excel
features.summary: A skill is a saved set of instructions that tells Copilot how to do one task your way. In Excel it is a folder in your OneDrive that holds one file called SKILL.md.
steps: In the Copilot pane, select the Settings menu (the ... in the upper-right corner).
Select Manage plugins & skills, then Custom skills.
Select Create OneDrive folder, then Open skills folder.
Copy your skill folders into that OneDrive folder.
Select Refresh in the Custom skills dialog so Copilot sees them.
To run one: select the Add menu in the prompt field, then Choose plugins and skills. Or type @ and the skill name.
prompts: @reconciliation-check Does this pack tie out?
@formula-risk-review Review the formulas in this model before I send it.
limits: The folder name must match the name inside SKILL.md, or Copilot skips the skill.
Turning a skill off in Manage plugins & skills stops automatic use. You can still run it with @.
The Microsoft page does not state licence or plan needs, and does not describe admin controls. Ask your IT team whether personal skills are allowed.
Skills that run Office.js scripts are a separate feature that Microsoft marks preview. None of these skills use scripts.

source.label: Use custom skills with Copilot in Excel (Microsoft Support)

features.title: Workbook structure audit
features.summary: Maps every sheet including hidden ones, named ranges, external links, filters and protection. Changes nothing.
steps: Select Download below and unzip the file.
Copy the folder workbook-structure-audit into your OneDrive skills folder.
In the Copilot pane in Excel, select Settings, then Manage plugins & skills, then Custom skills, then Refresh.
Open your workbook, then type @workbook-structure-audit in the Copilot prompt field.
prompts: What is actually in this workbook?
I inherited this file, map it for me
Are there hidden sheets or external links in here?
limits: Describes the file only. It never unhides, unfilters or unprotects anything.
It does not open or follow external links. It lists them as written.
If it cannot read something, it says unknown, not none.
Community skill, not from Microsoft. Use it first on a copy of a workbook with no sensitive data.
